commits.message:
Return typed finalized deployment manifests from core

Move the complete structural manifest type into core and return it from
finalized verification. Migrate node, fault-proofs, watcher, DA, and tooling
consumers while preserving verification rules and object ownership.

Add direct verifier rejection and ownership coverage. Correct the watcher
timeout expectation and synchronize the supervisor deadline test with actual
runner entry, retaining production timeout and deadline enforcement.

Validation: workspace pnpm test (all lanes green), full DA suite, built core
exports, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, and standards/spec reviews.
Complete shared assembly migration for remaining cursor families
Fix funding-wallet authority in emulator reference publication

Derive workflow runner factories from total linear family definitions

Remove crossBlockDuplicateEvent from the linear spec because its production
workflow uses the cursor adapter. Require a definition for every linear
category and delete the temporary migration allow-list.

Derive all 18 linear runner factories from the definitions table, retaining
module-private admission and the dedicated DA hash preimage launch route.
Remove the repeated exported constructors and update registration source
paths without changing statuses or reasons. Watcher imports those removed
constructors, so switch its call sites to the corresponding factory rows.

Validation (Node 22.23.1, pnpm 9.15.4):
- Rebuilt gitignored plutus.json with aiken v1.1.23+5adf783 build --env testnet
  before checks; 1149 entries, cross-block parameter lists match source.
- Typecheck: fault-proofs, watcher, node, node-tools.
- Lint: fault-proofs and the changed watcher file; changed-file formatting.
- Vitest: manifest-bound-family-assembly, workflow, workflow-runtime,
  linear-family-state, cursor-family-state, cursor-family-adapter,
  da-hash-preimage: 7 files / 520 tests passed.
- Additional cross-block-installed-lifecycle and
  submit-init-emulator-da-hash-preimage: 8 failures. All 8 also fail on the
  pre-change a1cc6a5de checkout with the freshly rebuilt blueprint; the
  underlying error is Invalid native script witness. A fresh blueprint
  alone does not resolve this emulator baseline failure in this environment.
- Admission loop and public generic-constructor rejection unchanged.

Refs #659, #657

Migrate the remaining linear families to the family assembly

Committed-field-shape, da-hash-preimage, double-withdraw, l2-tx-mistag,
withdrawn-reference-input and native-inclusion-two-step each declare a
family definition and reduce their constructor to the manifest-bound
assembly. Native-inclusion-two-step yields the invalidRange and zeroInput
definitions over one shared transaction port; both keep their constructor
names.

The linear definitions table now holds eighteen of the nineteen linear
categories. The allow-list shrinks to crossBlockDuplicateEvent, whose spec
row is linear but whose live workflow runs on the cursor adapter; moving it
onto the cursor arm or out of the linear spec is a separate decision.

The table test's certificate case now checks what the flag controls: the
certificate mint reference binding and the manifest refusal. Two of the
migrated ports read the certificate policy id into a step verdict without
binding the minting script, exactly as before the migration.

Assemble the receive-purpose-language cursor family from a family definition

Generalise the family definition so one definition type serves both adapter
arms: the linear arm keeps taking its step contract names and chain shape
from the linear family spec, while the cursor arm carries the cursor spec,
its step contract names, the optional action refiner and the cursor
transaction port. A fourth StepCount parameter, inferred from the cursor
spec's literal step count, sizes the cursor arm's step tuples the way the
linear spec's tuple sizes a linear arm's. Every Linear* name stays as an
alias over the family-wide type with the same parameters.

The assembly builds the cursor adapter from that arm with
createCursorFamilyWorkflowAdapter instead of throwing, and checks that a
cursor arm's spec agrees with its category and step contract names.

Move receive-purpose-language onto the assembly: the family's constructor
becomes a check of its callback-free config and decision digest followed by
the assembly, `extend` supplies the actuator, lucid instance and state-queue
lease coordinator the family's runner needs, and the constructor attaches
the invocation-bound decision digest. A sibling CURSOR_FAMILY_DEFINITIONS
table and a combined FAMILY_DEFINITIONS table sit beside the untouched linear
table, and the table-driven assembly test now covers both arms generically.

Refs #658

Migrate the witness and fee linear families onto the family assembly

Canonical-decodability, invalid-signature, min-fee and
input-set-uniqueness are reduced to their transaction port plus a frozen
family definition; the per-family constructor and run-or-resume names
remain as aliases over the assembly, and the config, workflow and
reference-script type names remain as aliases over the generic types.
Every field-carriage and proof-chunk callback moves verbatim, including
the forced-artifact branches that skip the membership proof and route
the forced field openings to steps 03 and 04. Input-set-uniqueness
declares two field-carriage requirements, spend plan then reference
plan, which the assembly applies in that order; min-fee declares its
nine per-field requirements from field 0 upward; all four declare the
field-preimage certificate.

Canonical-decodability's transaction port resolves the authenticated
field carriage itself before it builds step 01, so the definition builds
the port a second stateless instance from the same requirement callback
the assembly decorates the adapter with.

Surface changes that ride along, none of which alters a submitted
transaction: canonical-decodability's prerequisites now follow the
assembly's fixed order, field carriage inside proof chunks, where the
hand-written body wrapped them the other way round, so its two step-01
publications swap order; the four proof-chunk ports now receive the
protocol maximum transaction size the assembly passes, so the direct
route's capacity fallback can engage; the configs accept the optional
replay context; the per-family "manifest omitted required contracts"
checks run when the transaction port is built, after reference binding,
and a missing certificate now fails with the assembly's message. The
input-set-uniqueness forced test's infrastructure-only key set gains the
replay context accordingly.

The definitions table gains the four entries in spec order, the
allow-list drops them, and the four workflow modules' census rows list
the assembly module.

Refs #656

Migrate the input-position linear families to the family assembly

Non-existent-input, input-no-idx, reference-input-no-idx and
withdrawn-input are reduced to their transaction port plus a frozen
family definition; the manifest-bound family assembly builds their
workflows. Each module keeps its constructor and type names as aliases
over the generic ones, so the runtime and the watcher import the same
surface as before. The field-carriage and proof-chunk callbacks move
into the definitions verbatim, including non-existent-input's forced
artifact branch, and the definitions table gains the four entries in
spec order while the allow-list of unmigrated families shrinks to twelve.

Three deliberate surface changes ride along, none of which changes any
submitted transaction. Input-no-idx, reference-input-no-idx and
withdrawn-input now hand the manifest's maxTxSize to the proof-chunk
prerequisite, as non-existent-input already did; without it the
direct-capacity classifier refused every fallback to chunked
publication. Their configs accept the optional replay context the
generic config carries. Withdrawn-input's "deployment chain is
incomplete" check runs when the transaction port is built, after
reference binding, instead of directly after the signer check.

Refs #655

Refuse activate-operator before the activation time instead of waiting

An activation attempted before the operator's activation time now fails
at once with a one-line refusal naming the activation time and the chain
time, in the shape the other operator entry verbs use, rather than
sleeping until the time arrives. Registering and activating in one verb
keeps its wait, since a fresh registration can never have reached its
time yet. Emulator tests cover the refusal and the activation once the
chain time is reached.

Bump lucid-evolution to 0.6.5 and test that a registration cannot prove its own duplication

lucid 0.6.5 (provider 0.2.4) makes the emulator apply the ledger's rule
that a transaction's reference inputs are disjoint from its inputs when a
PlutusV3 script runs, so the emulator now refuses a duplicate-operator
slash whose proof is the node being removed, exactly as the ledger does.
The operator-exit emulator suite asserts that refusal.

The workspace patch on lucid moves to the 0.6.5 key; it applies
unchanged. The nine packages that pin lucid move together.

Assemble manifest-bound linear family workflows from one definition table

One assembly module now builds a linear family's manifest-bound workflow
from a frozen family definition: bind the verified manifest, check the
signer, bind every spec step and declared witness reference script (and
the field-preimage certificate mint when declared), start the L1
observation port, build the family's transaction port and adapter, then
apply the declared prerequisites in a fixed order, field carriage before
proof chunks. A generic run-or-resume hands the workflow's replayer,
single-category launch scope, terminal verifier and release-finality
authority to the retained-DA runner.

The definition is separate from the linear family spec and keyed by
category; step contract names come from the spec and are never
re-declared. It carries step datum schemas, witness roles, the
replayer, the adapter arm (linear implemented, cursor typed but not yet
assembled), one or more field-carriage requirement callbacks, an
optional proof-chunk callback and an optional extend hook. Spec steps
are now tuple-typed so a family's step count is visible to the
reference-script types.

Fabricated deposit, fabricated withdrawal and no-reference-input are
reduced to their transaction port plus definition; their constructor and
type names remain as aliases over the generic ones. Two deliberate
surface changes ride along: the fabricated families' configs now accept
the optional replay context the generic config carries, and their
"manifest omitted required contracts" check runs when the transaction
port is built, after reference binding, instead of directly after the
signer check. Neither changes any submitted transaction. The definitions
table carries a satisfies guard against the linear category list behind
an explicit allow-list of the sixteen families still to migrate.

A table-driven test replaces the two-family fabricated reference-binding
test: fake deployment binding, exact reference binding before provider
startup, missing/moved/forged refusals, declared-prerequisite chain
order and the retained-DA runner hand-off, for every migrated family.
Glossary gains "family definition" and "manifest-bound family assembly".

Refs #654

Operator exit, watchdog and status, with in-flight watcher and fault-proof work

Operator lifecycle (node, SDK, docs): voluntary and forced retirement,
duplicate-registration slashing, bond recovery, scheduler rewind onto
the surviving tail, inactivity strikes with the strike-cap refusal, the
operator watchdog fiber (on by default, OPERATOR_WATCHDOG_ENABLED and
OPERATOR_WATCHDOG_PATIENCE_MS, slot-aware deferral, manifest verified
at start), GET /operator/status with nextPatienceTakeoverTime, the
funding preflight, exact-fee construction with the three-coin collateral
cap, and lucid-evolution emulator suites in both polarities.

A lone registration cannot prove its own duplication: the proof is a
reference input and the removed node is an input, and the ledger keeps
the two disjoint. The validator, node and docs now state that rule as
the guarantee. The emulator-side negative test lands with the lucid pin
bump that carries the emulator fix.

Also included: the finalizer Q56/Q58 local readiness gates removed per
the release-plumbing simplicity ruling, and the in-flight watcher,
fault-proof, node-tools, da-committee-node and core changes from the
parallel sessions. All packages typecheck; the seven operator suites
pass; the other packages' suites were not rerun for this commit.
Record the five families with completed live watcher journeys

Requeue a fault-proof job whose run failed before its journal

The supervisor marked every run finished in the queue journal, including
one that threw before writing a single workflow record. The next process
then computed the same job identity, read the durable finish, and never
ran the proof again while the watcher reported ready. Leave a failed
run's registration active so the next process requeues it, and reopen a
finished registration whose workflow directory holds no execution.

Bind the complete-replay historical corpus to the block, not one object

The header classifier admits the historical native-script corpus against
the evidence it routed, but a family workflow that reuses that admitted
context re-fetches the same challenged block from retained DA. The corpus
check compared the two evidence objects by identity and refused the live
mintAuthorization workflow with 'historical corpus was not admitted for
this challenged header'. Compare the header hash and payload digests
instead, as the predecessor authority already does.
